newsitem.title: FRANCE: French policeman suspected of Basque ETA ties.
newsitem.headline: French policeman suspected of Basque ETA ties.

text.p: A French police officer in the Mediterranean port city of Marseille was in custody on Thursday on suspicion of links to the Basque separatist movement, judicial sources said.
They said the officer, whose name was not disclosed but who had previously been posted in Paris, had been arrested at his Marseille home on Tuesday morning and held after questioning.
He may be taken before an anti-terrorism magistrate in Paris on Friday, the sources added.
They said the officer's name had turned up on a computer disc seized after last week's arrest in southern France of suspected Basque ETA rebel leader Juan Luis Aguirre Lete.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed some 800 people in the 28 years it has been struggling for Basque independence.
At the time of Aguirre Lete's arrest, police found a cache of documents including a compilation of possible targets.
On the list of targets were French Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre and former interior minister Charles Pasqua, French police said.
Spain applauded Aguirre Lete's arrest, saying it had led to the dismantling of a rebel squad that had been planning attacks in the Navarre region of Spain.
